newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR staff to pull out of east Zaire refugee area.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR staff to pull out of east Zaire refugee area.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Friday it planned to evacuate staff from the refugee area in east Zaire because of reports of rebel advances, raising doubts over a planned trip to the region by UNHCR chief Sadako Ogata.

Spokesman Fernando Del Mundo said UNHCR was reviewing the situation "hour by hour" and could not say when the evacuation by air would happen. "We're considering evacuation of our staff by air but we cannot say when," he said.

A trip by Ogata, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, who arrived in Zaire's capital Kinshasa on Friday on the first leg of a week-long tour of the troubled Great Lakes region, to the region depended on security, he added.
Fighting between rebels and Zairean troops threatens another exodus in Lubutu region, home to 200,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in the middle of the rainforest.
Del Mundo said four UNHCR staff in Lubutu would be pulled to east Zaire's regional hub of Kisangani but could not say when.

In Lubutu, 200 km (125 miles) southeast of Kisangani, there are 120,000 refugees in Tingi-Tingi camp and another 40,000 in Amisi. Some 40,000 refugees who were in nearby Shabunda camp are now on the run after the rebels seized the village this week.
"We will pull our staff out of Lubutu. Air evacuation is being planned. We are looking at the situation hour by hour," Del Mundo said.
He said UNHCR had reports of refugees fleeing Amisi camp towards Tingi-Tingi to the northwest but Tingi-Tingi camp was reported calm as of Friday morning.
U.N. sources said in Nairobi that the 24 U.N. staff at Tingi Tingi camp would be "relocated" to Kisangani before rebel forces arrived.
"It is very dangerous, it seems," a U.N. source told Reuters. "We already hear from some sources there might be fighting in Lubutu so a road trip for staff is out. They have to come out by air."
Other aid sources said 170 wounded Zairean soldiers were evacuated from Amisi to Lubutu on Thursday and U.N. staff in Kisangani were told to stay in their homes or offices on Friday.
Del Mundo said UNHCR staff in Kisangani were working normally and could not confirm the reports on wounded Zairean soldiers.
Zairean defence officials acknowledged the fall of the town of Shabunda on Wednesday but played down the impact of the rebel advance, saying they had had only a few soldiers in the area.
They have acknowledged a rebel thrust into mineral-rich Shaba province in the southeast and the fall of Kalemie there.
But they hotly denied rebel claims to be near Lubutu town on the road to Kisangani, headquarters for an army counter-offensive launched on January 20, and Isoro to the north east.
Aid workers reported on Thursday some refugees were leaving Amisi, 80 km (50 miles) down the road from Lutubu to the rebel -held east. Other sources reported fighting close to a refugee camp there.
Zairean officials said the refugees had been panicked by rumours. "They are fleeing because of rumours," one said.

Relief officials have expressed increasing concern at the plight of several hundred thousand Hutus trapped by the fighting after fleeing west in December with the Rwandan Hutu hardliners, who were blamed for the 1994 genocide of Tutsis in Rwanda.
